learning: Iteration 2 showed the 10 cm span fixed oval losses but not slalom or s-bend. The Builder's wheel_track test is the next variable. If oscillation rises above 0.3 with losses still present, the next Integrator lever is kd or kp, and the Builder's lever is the footprint or sensor layout.
notes: Integrated the Builder's wheel_track 0.10 m drivetrain test with the 10 cm sensor span. kp is lowered to 0.9 to offset the sharper turn response and limit the oscillation rise seen in iteration 2.
rationale: Iteration 2 is the best evidence so far (score 124.6). Widening the span to 10 cm (outer sensors at ±0.05 m) cut oval line losses from 1.0 to 0.05 per run, but slalom stayed at 1.0 and s-bend at 0.9, with max_error still about 0.061 to 0.064 m. Steering oscillation rose to 0.23 to 0.27 on oval and s-bend, above the 0.08 to 0.16 seen before. The Builder's proposal changes one variable, wheel_track from 0.12 m to 0.10 m, which is the drivetrain branch the Integrator specified for persistent losses. I keep that geometry unchanged. Turn rate is the wheel speed difference divided by wheel_track, so a 0.10 m track gives about 20 percent more turn authority for the same wheel command. To avoid adding overcorrection on top of the oscillation already seen, I reduce kp from 1.0 to 0.9. That leaves the effective steering gain near 1.08 times the 0.12 m value, not 1.2 times. kd 0.2 stays to damp the faster response. ki 0.05, base_speed 1.0 and last_direction stay as they were, so this race changes only the drivetrain and the one gain that compensates for it. Expected result: slalom and s-bend line losses fall below 1.0 per run, and steering_oscillation stays below about 0.3. Runs are still unlikely to finish within 3 s at base_speed 1.0, so completion_time remains a constraint to watch.
